title: The Scholarship of Lake Minnow
premise: Ada Okafor, a scholarship student who has spent seven years perfecting the art of being overlooked, is paired for a semester project with Theo Marsh — the boy whose family's name is on the school and whose grandfather helped bury the truth about what lies beneath Lake Minnow Academy. Their research into the school's founding uncovers evidence that Ada's own father, once a groundskeeper here, was blamed for a drowning that Theo's family covered up. As the two rivals dig deeper, they must decide whether exposing the truth will cost Ada his scholarship, Theo his inheritance, and both of them the fragile belonging they've finally found. The story ends at the academic decathlon championship, where Ada uses his final presentation not to win the trophy but to tell the whole school what happened under the lake — and Theo stands up beside him, choosing truth over legacy.
about_author: Xanthe Brightwater grew up in a lake town where every local claimed to know what was at the bottom, and no two stories matched. She writes young adult novels about kids who discover that institutions keep secrets the way water keeps bodies — patiently, and not forever.

chapters.title: The Rules of Being Invisible
chapters.summary: Ada Okafor's POV. On his first day back at Lake Minnow Academy, Ada narrates his seven-year system for staying unseen: sit center-left, never first, never last. But a new scholarship audit letter hints his funding depends on 'community contribution.' Emotional beat: anxious control beginning to crack.

chapters.title: Nemesis, Assigned
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ms. Ferreira announces semester research pairs, and Ada is matched with Theo Marsh — the boy who mocked him freshman year and whose family built the school. Theo looks as horrified as Ada feels. Emotional beat: dread laced with reluctant curiosity about why Theo hates him too.

chapters.title: What the Lake Keeps
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo resents being paired with 'the charity case,' but the project topic — the school's founding — forces him into the archive where his grandfather's name appears on documents that don't add up. Emotional beat: inherited pride wobbling for the first time.

chapters.title: Truce Terms
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The rivals negotiate a coldly professional partnership: split the work, no personal questions. In the archive basement, Ada finds a 1998 photo of groundskeepers — including a young man with his father's face. Emotional beat: a jolt of recognition he hides from Theo.

chapters.title: The Drowning Year
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo discovers a sealed incident report from 1998: a student drowned in Lake Minnow, and a groundskeeper named Okafor was dismissed without charges. He realizes Ada's father is the man his family blamed. Emotional beat: guilt arriving before understanding.

chapters.title: Two Kinds of Scholarship
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada confronts his mother, who begs him to leave the past buried — his father lost everything once already. Meanwhile the decathlon coach recruits Ada, promising the championship could secure his future. Emotional beat: loyalty pulling against the itch of truth.

chapters.title: The Boathouse Agreement
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo corners Ada at the boathouse and admits what he found, offering a deal: finish the project quietly, then part ways. Ada refuses to sign away the truth. Their argument is interrupted by Headmaster Voss, who watches them a beat too long. Emotional beat: alliance forming out of mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: Decathlon Drills
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Decathlon training becomes Ada's refuge — the one place effort is rewarded openly. Teammate Priya befriends him, the first real friend in seven years, and asks why he flinches whenever Theo's family is mentioned. Emotional beat: belonging tasted and immediately endangered.

chapters.title: Grandfather's Ledger
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Searching his grandfather's study, Theo finds a ledger with payments labeled 'Minnow settlement' continuing for years after the drowning — hush money, or something worse. His father catches him and orders him to drop the project topic. Emotional beat: filial duty curdling into doubt.

chapters.title: The Girl in the Photograph
chapters.summary: Shared POV alternating scenes. The pair tracks down the drowned student's identity: Lena Whitfield, sixteen, whose family left town overnight. A retired librarian remembers Lena was dating someone 'important' that summer. Emotional beat: grief given a face, stakes made human.

chapters.title: Audit
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Headmaster Voss summons Ada, warning that 'distractions' threaten his enrollment — an unmistakable threat dressed as concern. Ada realizes the school has been watching them. Emotional beat: fear weaponized; Ada must choose between safety and the story.

chapters.title: Priya's Question
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Priya discovers Ada's secret research and feels betrayed that he hid it while she shared her own struggles freely. Their friendship fractures. Emotional beat: the cost of secrecy — Ada repeating the isolation he swore he'd escaped.

chapters.title: The Storm Drain
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Following an old maintenance map, Theo and Ada find a storm drain beneath the boathouse leading toward the lakebed — and signs it was sealed in a hurry in 1998. Someone has been inside recently. Emotional beat: the mystery turns physical and dangerous.

chapters.title: Midnight in the Archive
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Breaking into the restricted archive at night, they find Lena Whitfield's actual autopsy notes: injuries inconsistent with drowning. They photograph everything — and trip a motion sensor. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration fused; no way back to invisibility.

chapters.title: Caught, Almost
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Voss interrogates them separately; each protects the other, and the lie cements their partnership into genuine trust. Theo confesses his childhood cruelty toward Ada, and Ada admits he'd hated Theo for reasons he never examined. Emotional beat: enemies becoming allies in earnest.

chapters.title: The Witness
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The librarian gives them a name: Lena's best friend, now living two towns over, who saw Theo's grandfather at the lake that night. She agrees to talk — if they can guarantee she won't be buried like the report was. Emotional beat: responsibility weighing on teenagers holding adults' secrets.

chapters.title: Legacy or Truth
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo confronts his dying grandfather, who neither confirms nor denies — but slips him a key to a safe-deposit box. Theo's father threatens to disown him if he keeps digging. Emotional beat: Theo choosing which inheritance actually matters.

chapters.title: The Box
chapters.summary: Shared POV. The safe-deposit box holds Lena's letters and a confession draft in the grandfather's handwriting — he covered up an accidental death caused by his son, Theo's father, then paid to keep it quiet. Emotional beat: devastation; the villain is closer than either boy imagined.

chapters.title: What Winning Is For
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. On the eve of the decathlon, Voss offers Ada anything — full ride, college connections — if he submits the sanitized project and stays silent. Ada thinks of his mother, his father's ruined name, Priya's forgiveness. Emotional beat: the temptation scene; Ada's answer is not yet no.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada competes brilliantly through the decathlon rounds, winning the crowd, the team, and Priya back by letting her in fully. Then he takes the stage for the final presentation — and abandons his approved script. Emotional beat: triumph repurposed as courage.

chapters.title: Everything Under the Lake
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Before the assembled school, Ada tells Lena's story; Theo walks onstage and corroborates it with the documents, naming his own father. Voss moves to stop them, but students rise, then teachers, then the librarian witness herself. Emotional beat: climax — justice spoken aloud outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: After the Water Clears
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Weeks later: an investigation opens, Theo's father resigns, and the school renames its scholarship fund for Lena Whitfield. Ada loses nothing he needed and gains everything he never let himself want — friends, a voice, a place. Final beat: Ada, no longer careful, dives into Lake Minnow and swims.
